narrative_purpose: Turns interdependent-network failure into an ecological sequence: remove animals without touching the forest, then watch pollination and seed dispersal fail, young plants vanish, and the remaining fauna lose food in return.
subject: A three-stage naturalist triptych of the same Pandoran forest clearing. First stage: abundant flying pollinators, woodsprites, grazers, and fruit-eating animals move among flowering and fruiting plants. Second stage: the mature vegetation still stands but the animals are absent; flowers remain unvisited, fruit drops and rots beneath parent plants, and no seeds travel into open ground. Third stage: the canopy is thinning, young plants are missing, flowers and fruit are scarce, and the few surviving animals are gaunt and leaving; both plant and animal bioluminescence has dimmed.
scene: One unchanged clearing followed through a coupled ecological collapse that begins with fauna loss rather than fire.
camera: Three matched eye-level landscape panels with the same trunks and rocks anchoring each time step.
light: First panel richly self-lit by living organisms, second panel dimmer despite intact trees, third panel cold and sparse with wide dark gaps.
palette: Cool cyan-teal life fading stage by stage; no broad warm fire because no tree is directly attacked.
style: Painterly speculative-ecology naturalist sequence, the same place observed over time.
detail_level: Crisp recurring landmarks and organisms so disappearances are obvious; backgrounds consistent across all stages.
composition: Three equal panels left to right, identical horizon and key trunks, open dark strips at the top and bottom for callouts.
consistency_notes: No trees are directly burned or cut. The visible collapse must proceed from animal absence to failed plant recruitment and then back to animal starvation.
negative_prompt: no text, no labels, no arrows, no fire, no chainsaws, no humans, no gore, no photographic or 3D-render look, no different locations between panels
